title: Positivity of mixed ample intersection numbers
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty proper $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] of dimension $d\geq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ be ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then the intersection number of [def-sc-intersection-number] satisfies
$$(L_1\cdots L_d\cdot X)>0.$$
The modules may be different, and $X$ need not be reduced, integral, equidimensional or smooth.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, lemma-ample-positive, applied with Z=X; statement and induction proof. The nonempty hypothesis is explicit here, as required by the definition of the intersection number.

proof.text: First record the closed-restriction convention used below. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a nonempty closed subscheme of a proper $k$-scheme, then $Z$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $i$ affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] makes every $i^*M_j$ ample when $M_j$ is ample. For any tensor product $M=\bigotimes_j M_j^{\otimes n_j}$, which is an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module, the canonical map $i_*\mathcal O_Z\otimes M\to i_*i^*M$ is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] applied to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Z$ (the schemes are of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian): on each open trivializing the finitely many invertible modules it is $i_*\mathcal O_Z\otimes\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$, multiplication, whose inverse sends $a$ to $a\otimes1$. The same node, applied to the coherent module $i^*M$ on $Z$, gives $H^q(Y,i_*i^*M)\cong H^q(Z,i^*M)$ for every $q$; these are the module cohomology groups of [def-pc-euler-characteristic], and the isomorphisms are natural, hence commute with multiplication by scalars of $k$ and are $k$-linear. Consequently their Euler polynomials agree, and [def-sc-intersection-number] gives $(M_1\cdots M_e\cdot Z)=(i^*M_1\cdots i^*M_e\cdot Z)$, where the right side is computed intrinsically on $Z$. This also applies to the empty list when $e=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BEP, definition-intersection-number, displayed equality and following explanation; Tag 0BEV, reduction from X to Z

proof.text: Prove simultaneously for every integer $e\geq0$, every nonempty proper $k$-scheme $Y$ of dimension $e$, and every list of $e$ ample invertible modules on $Y$, that its mixed intersection number is positive. Induct on $e$. For $e=0$, [def-sc-intersection-number] says that the empty intersection is $\chi(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] to the coherent module $\mathcal O_Y$, whose support is $Y$: this is $\dim_k\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. The unit section is nonzero since $Y$ has a point with a nonzero local ring. Thus $k\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is injective and this dimension is at least one. This proves the base case over every field.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, induction base d=0 using Tag 0AYT, lemma-chi-tensor-finite

proof.text: Let $e>0$ and assume the asserted positivity for all nonempty proper schemes of dimension $e-1$. For a scheme $Y$ of dimension $e$ and a list $M_1,\ldots,M_e$, apply [lem-sc-top-dimensional-reduction-intersection] with $Z=Y$. It expresses the intersection as $\sum_j m_j(M_1\cdots M_e\cdot Y_j)$ over the reduced integral top-dimensional components, with $m_j>0$. There is at least one such component, since $\dim Y=e$; the finite top-component list in that lemma has maximum dimension $e$. Step 1 makes each $Y_j$ proper, each restricted $M_i$ ample, and identifies the ambient and intrinsic numbers. It therefore suffices to prove positivity for an integral $Y$ of dimension $e$. This is a reduction within the current induction step, not an appeal to induction in the same dimension.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, reduction to integral Z via Tag 0BES, lemma-intersection-number-in-terms-of-components

proof.text: Now $Y$ is integral and nonempty. Choose $y\in Y$. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], applied to $M_1$ at $y$, there are $r\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M_1^{\otimes r})$ such that $y\in Y_s$ and $Y_s$ is affine. In particular $s\ne0$. Put $N=M_1^{\otimes r}$. Repeated tensor additivity from [lem-sfb-top-intersection-multilinear] gives $(N M_2\cdots M_e\cdot Y)=r(M_1M_2\cdots M_e\cdot Y)$, by induction on the positive integer $r$. Since $r>0$, proving positivity of the left side proves positivity of the required number. The other $e-1$ modules have not been changed.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, positive tensor power using Tag 0BER and an affine nonvanishing open using Properties Tag 01PS

proof.text: The zero scheme $D=Z(s)$ is nonempty. Indeed, if it were empty, the nonvanishing locus would be all of $Y$, making $Y$ affine. Then [lem-sc-proper-affine-finite-general] makes $Y$ finite over $k$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] gives $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite-dimensional over $k$. Every prime quotient $B/\mathfrak p$ is a finite-dimensional domain: multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective, so the quotient is a field. Every prime is therefore maximal and $\dim Y=0$, contradicting $e>0$. The underlying support of $Z(s)$ is exactly $Y\setminus Y_s$: in a local trivialization both conditions say that the coefficient of $s$ belongs to the point's prime ideal.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, nonemptiness of Z(s), using Morphisms Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper

proof.text: Since $Y$ is integral and $s\ne0$, [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier] makes $D$ an effective Cartier divisor. Apply [lem-sc-intersection-effective-cartier] with ambient scheme and closed subscheme both $Y$, first module $N$, remaining modules $M_2,\ldots,M_e$, and divisor $D=Z(s)$. Its zero-section clause supplies $N\cong\mathcal O_Y(D)$, and its integral alternative applies without any prior dimension assertion about $D$. It gives that $D$ is proper with $\dim D=e-1$ and that $(N M_2\cdots M_e\cdot Y)=(M_2\cdots M_e\cdot D)$. By Step 1, the right side is the intrinsic intersection for the ample restrictions $M_2|_D,\ldots,M_e|_D$.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, regular zero divisor and its dimension; Tag 0BEU, lemma-numerical-intersection-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: The induction hypothesis now applies to the nonempty proper scheme $D$ of dimension $e-1$ and its $e-1$ ample restricted modules. Its intersection number is positive, including the empty-list case when $e=1$. Step 6 and the positive scalar $r$ in Step 4 give positivity for integral $Y$. Substituting these positive numbers into the sum with positive multiplicities in Step 3 gives positivity for arbitrary $Y$. This completes the induction. Take $Y=X$ and $e=d$ to obtain the item.

source.place: Tag 0BEV, final induction step and assembly after component reduction
